first.rationale: Aggressive competitor pricing creates an immediate, segment-specific threat to qualified SMB acquisition. Promotional pricing has prior evidence of acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMBs, but its effects on margin, retention, and customer quality must be checked before acting because the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Onboarding simplification is also verified as the strongest alternative because completion is declining and it may address activation indirectly.

final.rationale: Run a shortened/simplified onboarding experiment. The verified source record showed completion up 13%, time-to-value 2.1 days faster, and 30-day retention up 3%, directly addressing the current 4% onboarding-completion decline while supporting sustainable qualified revenue through earlier adoption and retention. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified acquisition and revenue lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline and was explicitly deemed unsustainable. Measure activation, qualified conversion, and retention by cohort as guardrails.
